title: QBR Playbook: Inference Economics & Availability for Enterprise Accounts
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:

This playbook defines a reproducible QBR (Quarterly Business Review) format focused on two topics that consistently drive value decisions for enterprise customers: inference economics (cost per call / cost per 1k tokens / embedding unit economics) and availability (SLOs, incidents, throttling/fallback). It is designed for Customer Success (CS) leads running QBRs with engineering stakeholders, finance owners, and product managers on the customer side.

When to use this playbook:
- Quarterly Business Reviews for enterprise and Dedicated/Private customers with non-trivial inference spend.
- Ad-hoc cost/availability deep-dives triggered by a cost spike, capacity incident, or contract renewal.
- Pre-renewal negotiating sessions where unit economics and reliability metrics inform pricing/commitments.

Audience:
- Customer Success Managers (owner)
- Solutions Engineers / Oncall Engineers (data/technical escorts)
- Account Finance / Procurement contacts (customer)
- Customer Platform/ML Engineers and Product Managers (customer)

QBR Objectives (measurable):
1. Verify that monthly inference unit cost trends match commitments and identify 2–3 concrete optimization actions.
2. Validate SLO adherence for the review period and document mitigation/rollout plans for any SLO misses.
3. Align on capacity requirements and recommended Dedicated/Private sizing changes (if required).
4. Agree on 3 follow-up action items with owners, deadlines, and acceptance criteria.

Standard QBR Agenda (60–90 minutes):
1) Welcome & goals (5 min)
2) Usage and unit economics snapshot (15 min)
   - Total tokens, embeddings units, average request size, and cost per 1k tokens
   - Cost drivers (model mix, quantization, caching hit-rate)
3) Availability and reliability review (15 min)
   - SLO metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, availability %)
   - Incidents since last QBR and RCA/high-level remediation status
4) Optimization opportunities and proposals (15 min)
   - Batching, caching rules, model switchover suggestions, routing policies
5) Roadmap & upcoming platform changes (10 min)
6) Action items, ownership, and close (5–10 min)

Pre-QBR Checklist (owner: Customer Success with Solutions Engineering support) – do these at least 10 business days before meeting:
- Data pulls: usage CSVs, token-level cost breakdown, model routing logs (last 90 days).
- Dashboards: ensure the customer-facing cost dashboard and availability dashboard are refreshed and have annotations for major incidents.
- Internal sync: Solutions Engineer and oncall review to identify technical risks and proposed recommendations.
- Customer pre-read: send a two-page summary (Key metrics + proposed agenda + 3 suggested actions).

Required Data Sources & Canonical Queries:
- Metric store: Prometheus / Cortex (latency, error-rate, availability per model/version)
- Billing: internal billing export (per-customer, per-model, per-day)
- Logs: request routing and model selection logs (to assess fallback frequency)

Example Prometheus queries (examples to run in dashboards):
- 95th percentile latency (tokens endpoint):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=~"/v1/generate.*",customer_id=\"<ID>\"}[7d])) by (le))

- Error rate (5m rolling):
  sum(rate(inference_requests_total{customer_id=\"<ID>\",status=~\"5..|4..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total{customer_id=\"<ID>\"}[5m]))

Sample billing CSV columns (expected):
- date, customer_id, model_name, model_variant, request_count, tokens_in, tokens_out, embedding_units, total_cost_usd

SLOs & KPI Table (Use these as baseline; adjust per-customer SLA):
- SLO name: Availability (per-route) | Target: 99.95% | Measurement: uptime excluding scheduled maintenance | Rollback threshold: <99.90%
- SLO name: P99 latency (text-generation) | Target: <= 1.2s per token at typical batch size | Measurement: p99 of token emission latency | Rollback threshold: >1.6s
- KPI: Cost per 1k tokens | Target: agreed contract baseline (e.g., $X / 1k tokens) | Measurement: billing export aggregated monthly

Action Playbook: Common Findings and Recommended Responses
1) Finding: Sudden 30% cost spike month-over-month with no obvious traffic increase.
   Steps:
   a) Verify billing export: group by model_variant and time-of-day to see concentrated increases.
   b) Check routing logs for increased fallback to larger models or degraded quantization usage.
   c) If fallback is the cause, enact short-term mitigation: route traffic to fallback limits, enable per-customer cost caps, and schedule canary switchover to a cheaper variant.
   d) Owner: Solutions Engineer (SE) to provide triage within 24 hours; CS to schedule cost remediation call within 3 business days.

2) Finding: P99 latency breach during daily peak windows.
   Steps:
   a) Confirm whether breach correlates with increased batch sizes or KV cache misses (run cache hit-rate query).
   b) If cache misses increased, review prefix caching rules and customer prompt patterns.
   c) Short-term: increase burst capacity or enable regional routing to lower latency.
   d) Long-term: propose model quantization or a smaller model for cheap paths.
   e) Owner: Oncall Engineer to propose mitigation within 48 hours; SE to test proposed fix in staging within 7 days.

3) Finding: Repeated transient 503s with no persistent service degradation.
   Steps:
   a) Cross-check ingress/load-balancer throttling metrics; validate whether request throttles align with customer quota thresholds.
   b) If quota throttles are the cause, recommend quota increase or implement client-side retry/backoff guidance.
   c) Owner: Customer Success to negotiate quota changes; Engineering to implement conservative quota bump and monitor.

Escalation Matrix (severity and contacts):
- Sev 1 (Critical production outage impacting >=1% of customer traffic or >30 minutes):
  - Primary oncall: eng-sre-oncall@redwood.ai (pager)
  - SE: solutions-oncall@redwood.ai
  - CS lead: <CS manager email>
  - Response SLA: 30 minutes initial response, incident channel created, daily exec updates.

- Sev 2 (High-impact but partial):
  - Eng oncall: eng-platform-oncall@redwood.ai
  - SE: assigned per-account
  - CS: assigned CSM
  - Response SLA: 2 hours initial response.

- Sev 3 (Low-impact / cost questions / non-urgent reliability trends):
  - Handle in the next business-day operating cadence; owner is CSM and Solutions Engineer.

Meeting artifacts & templates (copy for reuse)
- Two-page pre-read template (send 3 business days before):
  1) Executive summary (1 paragraph): top-line cost delta, availability summary, 1 recommended action.
  2) Key metrics: last 3 months trend charts (tokens, cost, p95/p99).
  3) Incidents & status: list of incidents since last QBR with RCA links.
  4) Proposed actions and impact estimate (e.g., expected cost reduction %).

- Action item tracker rows (example):
  - \"Reduce model X usage on low-cost paths\" | Owner: SE-Jordan | ETA: 2026-03-15 | Acceptance: 10% cost reduction in low-cost path within 30 days

Follow-up & tracking:
- All action items must be captured in the CS ticketing system (Zendesk/Jira) with a label qbr-<customer-id>-YYYYQn.
- CS to run a 30-day follow-up email with progress and updated metrics visualization.
- If cost or availability objectives are not met within 60 days, schedule a remediation game-day with engineering (2 hours) to drive higher-priority fixes.

Appendix A — Sample queries and scripts
- Cost breakdown extraction (example CSV extractor):
  curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>\" 
    \"https://billing.internal.redwood.ai/v1/exports?customer_id=<ID>&start=2026-01-01&end=2026-02-28\" > billing-<ID>-jan-feb.csv

- KV cache hit rate example (PromQL):
  sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{customer_id=\"<ID>\"}[7d])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{customer_id=\"<ID>\"}[7d]))

Appendix B — Suggested optimization playbacks (examples to present)
- Batching policy change: expected savings 8–18% for chat-heavy workloads; risk: increases p99 latency for tail callers.
- Prefix caching rules: expected savings 12–30% when customers use repeated system prompts.
- Quantized model recommendation: move 20% of low-sensitivity traffic to a 4-bit quantized variant to reduce cost 25–40% (requires QA for accuracy regression).
